data.content_ref: inline:The target's own countercondition betrays an internal incoherence. Countercondition 2 states that the account fails 'if resilience in the past is logically irrelevant to resilience in the future without an inductive bridge.' Yet the mechanism explicitly asserts that the account 'avoids induction because it makes no claim about the future, only a comparative claim about the past record of resilience.' If the account genuinely makes no future claim whatsoever, then the logical irrelevance of past resilience to future resilience cannot possibly undermine it—the account would stand regardless, since it professes to be silent on the future. The fact that the target identifies this irrelevance as a failure condition reveals that the account's viability secretly depends on there being some meaningful connection between past resilience and future performance—the very inductive bridge the mechanism denies. The countercondition presupposes the bridge the mechanism repudiates.
